about.title: Lathrop Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Lathrop's growth along I-5 and Harlan Road has brought in more warehouses, distribution centers, and retail traffic — which means more products moving through the area, and more chances for a defective one to reach a household in San Joaquin County. Whether it's a faulty appliance, a piece of industrial equipment, a vehicle part, or a household tool that failed the way it shouldn't have, California's strict liability rules mean an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That can apply to a manufacturer, a distributor, or the retailer who sold it. If a product hurt you or someone in your family here in Lathrop, holding onto the item itself and any packaging matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect people who've been hurt with an independent attorney who can review what happened and explain the options, at no cost to start.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters in a Lathrop Product Claim

items.title: No Need to Prove Carelessness
items.desc: Under California's strict liability rules, you generally don't have to show the manufacturer was negligent — just that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties Can Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers who sold the product may all share liability, which can matter with the number of warehouses and retail outlets along Lathrop's I-5 corridor.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Keeping the defective item, its packaging, and any receipts intact gives an attorney the evidence needed to show how the defect caused harm.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: No. California strict liability law generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective and whether that defect caused your injury, not on what the manufacturer knew or intended. This is different from a typical negligence claim.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was when the injury happened, along with any packaging, instructions, or receipts. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away — an independent attorney will want to have it examined.

items.question: Does it matter that I bought the product from a retailer near Harlan Road or Stanford Crossing rather than the manufacturer directly?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law allows claims against retailers and distributors, not just the original manufacturer, so where you purchased the product in Lathrop doesn't eliminate your options.
